title: Take Gifts From the Richest Pile
summary: Given an array of integers representing the number of gifts in each pile, every second select the pile with the most gifts, then reduce its gift count to the square root of its current count, rounded down.
statement: Given an array of integers representing the number of gifts in each pile, every second select the pile with the most gifts, then reduce its gift count to the square root of its current count, rounded down. Repeat this process k times and return the final gift count for each pile.
constraints: Each step chooses a currently largest pile and replaces it with floor(sqrt(pile)).
Return the sum of all pile sizes afterward.
hints: A max-priority queue is needed because every step selects the current largest pile.
Store negated sizes in Python’s min-heap.
Pop the largest, replace it by integer square root, push it back, and finally sum.
Heap extraction enforces the required greedy choice at every step, so the simulation matches the process exactly.

tests.explanation: Repeatedly reducing the current largest piles leaves a total of twenty-nine gifts.
The square root of one is one, so the total remains four.
